  • In a recent development, le 31 août 2023, il est prêté au club luxembourgeois de l'Union Titus Petange pour la saison 2023-2024.

Recent findings suggest that L'ancien Vert, Mathys Saban opère désormais au Mâcon 71 (N2), après un passage au Luxembourg (Titus Petange, Racing FC Union). Au sortir d’une crise interne marquée par une grève de l’entraînement, Mâcon 71 jouait un match key sur le terrain de la réserve d'Annecy. À dix contre onze (après l'exclusion de l'ancien Vert, Israël Kinunga) et après avoir été rattrapé sur penalty, les Mâconnais ont montré qu’ils savaient réagir. C'est Mathys Saban, entré en jeu à la 71ème, qui a donné la victoire (1-2) aux siens, à la toute dernière minute du match. Un autre ancien Vert, Yoann Greco est entré en jeu à la 65ème.Avec 11 points, Mäcon 71 pointe à la 7ème place, à 8 points du leader Bourgoin dans le championnat de N2.

In a recent development, mathys Saban (24 ans), joueur offensif polyvalent, est arrivé au centre de Formation de l'ASSE en 2017, en provenance de l'US Torcy qui a fourni aux Verts Lamine Ghezali, Alexandre Valbon, Josué Gago et Marwan Nzuzi, Lucas Gourna-Douath, Mathis Amougou, Fodé Camara, Axel Dodote. Il a gravi toutes les étapes de la formation et signé son premier contrat pro de 3 ans avec l'ASSE le 5 juin 2020, contrat qui sera prolongé de 2 ans en février 2023.En 2020-2021, il joue son premier match en pro, le 23 mai 2021, 12 minutes lors de ASSE-Dijon : 0-1.En 2021-2022, il participe à 3 matchs de Ligue 1 : - 21 août 2021, 21 minutes : ASSE-LOSC : 1-1- 28 août 2021 : 19 minutes : OM-ASSE : 3-1- 12 septembre 2021 : 30 minutes : Montpellier-ASSE : 2-0En 2022-2023, il participe à 3 matchs de Ligue 2 qui se soldent par 3 défaites, et 1 match en Coupe de France : - le 29 octobre 2022, Coupe de France, 30 minutes : ASSE-Rodez : 0-0 (3-4 tab)- le 7 novembre 2022, 45 minutes, Metz-ASSE : 3-2- le 12 novembre 2022, 17 minutes : ASSE-Rodez : 0-2  - le 26 décembre 2022, 33 minutes : Annecy-ASSE : 2-1.

In a recent development, le 31 août 2023, il est prêté au club luxembourgeois de l'Union Titus Petange pour la saison 2023-2024. Victime d’une rupture du tendon d’achille au début du printemps 2024 lors de son prêt à l’Union Titus Pétange, Mathys Saban revient à l'ASSE pour la saison 2024-2025 mais ne joue que 77 minutes en N3 pour sa 8ème et dernière saison sous le maillot vert. Il retourne  dans le Grand-Duché durant l'été 2025 (au Racing Football Club Union Lëtzebuerg), et inscrit en septembre 2025 son premier but en L1 luxembourgeoise. Malheureusement son contrat est rompu début 2026 et, après 6 mois sans club, il rejoint donc le Mâcon 71 qui a raté de peu l'accession au Championnat National, devancé par Hauts Lyonnais.

Commenté par Jérémy Clément, le match du 8e tour de Coupe de France que les Verts joueront contre le FC Villefranche Beaujolais ce samedi à 19h00 dans le Chaudron sera diffusé sur les comptes Facebook de France 3 Alpes, France 3 Auvergne et France 3 Rhône-Alpes ainsi que sur la chaîne YouTube France TV - ICI Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes.

Pour rappel, l'ancien numéro 6 de l'ASSE avait déjà commenté sur France 3 un match de Coupe de France des Verts il y a 3 ans. Malgré les efforts de l'actuel milieu de terrain dunkerquois Jordan Morel, Bourg-Péronnas s'était incliné 0-3 face aux hommes de Laurent Batlles (but de Maxence Rivera, doublé de Gaëtan Charbonnier).

Comme l'a annoncé Florent Houzot, le tirage au sort des 32èmes de finale de Coupe de France aura lieu lundi prochain dès 19h00 et sera diffusé en direct par beIN Sports.

Fiorentina e Milan pagano 5mila euro ciascuna; provvedimenti anche per Atalanta, Genoa, Monza, Udinese e Bologna.

Il Giudice sportivo ha inflitto 10.000 euro di ammenda alla Roma per oggetti lanciati dai suoi sostenitori durante la gara e 8.000 euro al Como per il ritardo di circa quattro minuti nell’inizio del secondo tempo. Secondo quanto riportato da Giudice sportivo, Sanzionate anche Fiorentina, Milan, Atalanta, Genoa, Monza, Udinese e Bologna.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, alla Roma sono contestati il lancio di tre petardi e di un accendino sul terreno di gioco, oltre a un fumogeno e una bottiglietta di plastica nel recinto di gioco. L’ammenda da 10.000 euro è stata attenuata ai sensi dell’articolo 29, comma 1, lettera b) del CGS.

Per l’Atalanta la sanzione è di 4.000 euro. I suoi sostenitori hanno lanciato un accendino sul terreno di gioco e due bottigliette nel recinto di gioco. Anche in questo caso l’ammenda è stata attenuata in base all’articolo 29, comma 1, lettera b) del CGS.

Il Como è stato multato di 8.000 euro a titolo di responsabilità oggettiva per aver provocato ingiustificatamente un ritardo di circa quattro minuti nell’inizio del secondo tempo. Il provvedimento segnala la recidiva reiterata.

In a recent development, ammende di 5.000 euro ciascuna per Fiorentina e Milan, sempre a titolo di responsabilità oggettiva. La Fiorentina ha causato ingiustificatamente un ritardo di circa due minuti nell’inizio del secondo tempo; il Milan, nella stessa fase della gara, un ritardo di circa tre minuti. Per entrambe è indicata la recidiva.

Il Genoa deve pagare 3.000 euro per aver provocato ingiustificatamente, a titolo di responsabilità oggettiva, un ritardo di circa due minuti nell’inizio del primo tempo. Stessa cifra per il Monza, al quale è contestato un ritardo ingiustificato di circa due minuti nell’inizio della ripresa, sempre a titolo di responsabilità oggettiva.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on upcoming players really does take some doing.

Sources indicate that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly released and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

According to recent reports, for Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he noted. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

Sources indicate that indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

Spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

Sources indicate that at the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi noted later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

Industry observers note that “There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

Spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This new stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

In a recent development, A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

In a recent development, hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Recent findings suggest that some surprised faces then when Moyes said later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”.

Recent findings suggest that the game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes mentioned that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”.

According to recent reports, in the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

According to recent reports, the first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

Recent findings suggest that de Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He said that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

Industry observers note that “We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender noted: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and revealed that mentality again in the second half.

“We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”.

Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

The Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

“We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” says Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

“I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’.

Recent findings suggest that “What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.

What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.

Celtic wins with bells and whistles attached have been as rare as hen’s teeth since this campaign began.

That the supporters witnessed one in trying circumstances felt significant given the arduous schedule which awaits in the coming six weeks.

Despite having no option but to piece together a midfield, O’Neill watched his side create a slew of opportunities. They took four with as many different scorers and might well have had more.

Industry observers note that A display brimming with enterprise and imagination boded well for what lies ahead. For the first time since September, Celtic have chalked up three straight wins. Ahead of the trip to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday, it appears that a bit of wind is back in the sails.

This was as comprehensive a win as the scoreline suggests. The champions were never in danger from the moment Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain edged them in front just after the half hour mark.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain celebrates Celtic's first goal against St Mirren.

It has been revealed that in danger of becoming something of a forgotten man, the former England man rolled back the years here with a display which reminded you why he once wore the shirts of Liverpool and Arsenal. On this evidence, he still has a contribution to make at Parkhead.

The outcome was more or less settled by the interval. Camilo Duran continued his outstanding first season in Glasgow’s East End with another assured finish.

Luke McCowan, a man who’s not exactly had his critics to seek in recent times, netted the third before the break, his goal a just reward for a tidy afternoon’s work.

On a day when O’Neill would have had concerns about his midfield, Callum McGregor also netted with a crisp strike from the edge of the box.

St Mirren’s consolation, coming from Killian Phillips’ penalty, was too little too late.

On Friday, Buddies boss Craig McLeish had made some salient points about the self-interest which is holding back Scottish football.

It’s hard not to like McLeish’s attitude and the style of football his side are playing. But they are continuing to lose goals far too easily. They could find themselves getting dragged into trouble if they don’t quickly address it.

Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring their second goal in the 4-1 win.

Sources indicate that on Friday, O’Neill had rejected the suggestion that Haissem Hassan had been omitted from the squad which faced Kilmarnock because he needed a kick up the backside. Yet, curiously, there was no sign of the Egyptian again here.

With Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur injured, O’Neill hoped that a combination of McGregor, McCowan and Oxlade-Chamberlain would have enough.

Recent findings suggest that kasper Hogh’s chances of ending a run of 16 games without a goal weren’t helped by him starting on the bench. He didn’t leave it.

With just one win in nine coming into this, Craig McLeish’s side were short on points yet they were not short on confidence.

Although they played some stuff which was very easy on the eye, an inability to keep the ball out of the net cost them dear again.

McCowan had an early shot blocked before Colby Donovan had a weak effort saved. McCowan also hesitated to take a first-time strike with Louis Jackson doing enough to protect Jacob Chapman’s goal.

Celtic actually had the ball in the net twice before they made it count. Duran planted a header and a shot in the visitors’ net only to discover that the offside flag had been raised.

Jota sparked a sweeping move which saw Yang Hyun-jun tee up McCowan. Paul Nsio became the latest Saints player to frustrate the Celtic midfielder with a block.

Saints were aggrieved that Yang won a free-kick by going to ground too easily just before the opener. They may have had a point. That didn’t excuse the defending which followed.

Cameron Carter-Vickers rolled the ball in Yang’s direction. The winger burst away from Declan John and assessed his options.

His cut-back for the unmarked Oxlade-Chamberlain was inch-perfect. The former England midfielder swept home his first goal since netting against the same opponent in April.

Industry observers note that saints might well have levelled immediately. Ismeal Kabia wriggled away from Donovan and picked out Eseosa Sule. Liam Scales did well to prevent the forward netting from seven yards.

Industry observers note that celtic then cut through Saints with embarrassing ease. A straight pass sent Yang clear on goal. He should have gone for glory, but instead tried to square the ball to allow Duran a tap-in. Alex Gogic had other ideas and knocked the ball away for a corner.

Celtic midfielder Luke McCowan and St Mirren's Paul Nsio battle for the ball.

McLeish’s hopes of making it to the break still in the contest unravelled in the final five minutes of the first period.

Sources indicate that kieran Tierney’s decision to swap flanks paid dividends with a brilliant in-swinging cross. Duran ghosted onto it and cushioned the ball beyond Chapman with his left foot to claim his 14th goal of his debut season.

Jota might well have made it three-nil seconds later and he fired Oxlade-Chamberlain’s lay-off straight at the keeper.

There was no hope for Chapman as Celtic all but wrapped up the win three minutes before the interval.

In a recent development, tierney was again the provider, his energy taking him to the line and allowing him to cross. McCowan calmly stroked home his second goal of the season.

Saints kept going seeking a goal which might have made it interesting. Kabia’s strike forced Sam Johnstone into a smart stop down to his right.

It has been revealed that yang ought to have killed the contest but blazed over while leaning back. Skipper McGregor showed him how to do it as he buried a right foot shot low in the bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the box after a defender had taken the ball off Duran’s toe.

Saints did get on the board thanks to Phillips’ penalty conversion, the award coming after Johnstone clattered Calvin Ramsay as he punched clear.

In a recent development, O’Neill was still able to send on Shim Mheaka and James Forrest with Austin Trusty returning to warm applause. Joel van den Berg had already been introduced for his debut along with Callum Osmand. The Dutch teenager demonstrated up well.

In a recent development, dans Le Patriote du Beaujolais, l'ancien gardien et capitaine caladois Franck Laurent se remémore son 16e de finale de Coupe de France perdu en aux tirs au buts contre les Verts (2-2, 1-3 tab). Extraits.

"Notre coach, Jean-Michel Picollet (photo), était à fond pour les Verts. C'était le derby pour nous. On était tellement contents de tomber sur eux ! Je me souviens encore de la causerie du coach, comme si c'était hier. Son message était clair et net. On allait respecter Saint-Etienne à 200% mais par contre, on allait jouer notre match à fond. Le coach nous disait qu'il y avait un truc à faire. Il nous avait mis dans cette position-là, mentalement on était prêt. On en a profité un maximum. Sur un match, on avait nos chances. On jouait sur notre terrain. Eux n'avaient pas l'habitude de ce genre de pelouse. Il y a des facteurs, dans ce genre de match, qui font que tu transcendes, que tu te mets au niveau de l'événement, tu joues ta chance à fond.

Industry observers note that ce match, on en parlait tous les jours entre nous. Du début à la fin, on a vécu les choses à fond ! Ce match-là, contre Saint-Etienne, ça fait 16 ans qu'il a été joué. On m'en parle régulièrement. Pourtant, je ne suis plus du tout dans le foot. Quand on se croise, entre joueurs de cette époque, les premiers mots portent toujours sur ce match. On est liés à vie avec cette aventure de Coupe de France. C'est un petit bout de l'histoire du FCVB. J'ai eu la chance d'être là, au bon moment. Dans une carrière, ce n'est pas si évident de laisser des traces pareilles dans un club !

Les conseils que je donnerais aux Caladois d'aujourd'hui avant d'aller à Geoffroy Guichard, ce samedi ? Le contexte est totalement différent. C'est une Ligue 2 contre une Ligue 3. Il y a des joueurs professionnels des deux côtés. Je ne sais pas si je peux leur donner un conseil, à mon niveau. Mais même pour eux, ça reste des matches magnifiques à vivre. J'espère qu'ils vont arriver à s'extraire du championnat pour profiter pleinement de ce match, et tout donner. Derrière, ça peut renforcer le groupe.".

Extraits.

Sources indicate that "Le président m’a proposé quelque chose d’inédit pour moi en me disant “je ne te veux pas pour mettre 40 buts par saison mais parce que j’ai beaucoup de bons jeunes qui vont monter et j’aimerais que tu les encadres, que tu les aides à se développer”. J’ai accepté direct. Je sortais de 7 saisons à Monistrol où j'ai connu 2 montées. Redescendre ce n’est pas grave, je donne plus d’importance au projet qu’au niveau.

Recent findings suggest that je parle beaucoup aux jeunes, j’essaye de les aider à passer le cap, je leur dis d’être patients quand ils jouent moins… Je suis toujours un peu décisif mais surtout content quand eux le sont. Je suis plus passeur que buteur maintenant, je préfère donner que marquer. J’ai un rôle de trentenaire, ça fait mal à dire (rires). Dimanche, en termes d’ambiance, je pense que ça va être un truc que je n’ai jamais vu. Ça va être extraordinaire.".

#118820. Giving Youri Tielemans a £35m release clause looks like an error... Aston Villa toiling to a draw with Sunderland was more proof Unai Emery could do with a midfield controller in January, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Giving Youri Tielemans a £35m release clause looks like an error... Aston Villa toiling to a draw with Sunderland was more proof Unai Emery could do with a midfield controller in January, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.
  • The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026.

Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.

The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.

Sources indicate that unai Emery was distraught to lose Tielemans and against Sunderland, you could see why. Emery signed two central midfielders, Leon Goretzka and Joao Gomes, and has given more minutes to Ross Barkley.

None of the three gives him what Tielemans did and Villa may decide to move for another central player in January. Anything for a bit of cleverness in that part of the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that tielemans has struggled at United and it will be interesting to see what Mauricio Pochettino makes of him. He is no elite athlete and United supporters and pundits have criticised him because of it but he gave Emery what he craves above all else – control. Neither Gomes nor Goretzka has Tielemans’ passing range and Barkley looks more effective higher up the pitch.

With Sunderland sitting deep here, Villa desperately needed a player who could read the game and create angles like Tielemans. Without him, their passing was slow and predictable, against a Sunderland side without key men Dominic Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey.

Sunderland's Nordi Mukiele stretches for the ball but nobody could find the breakthrough.

Regis Le Bris saw his side pick up another point to follow their win over Chelsea before the international break - Sunderland now sit 18th.

Industry observers note that their only chance in the first half here fell to Emi Buendia, who won the ball high then failed to chip the back-pedalling Robin Roefs. In the second half, Ian Maatsen and substitute Ibrahim Mbaye shot far too close to the Sunderland goalkeeper, who tipped over another effort from Barkley.

Villa have still not lost in the league since they were beaten here by Nottingham Forest in September but teams aiming for the Champions League should put away Sunderland at home. And after 150 Premier League games at the helm, nobody will know that better than Emery.

Buendia reached Aston Villa immortality last May when he scored in the Europa League final and now he has his own banner.

‘It’s Buendia, with a beauty, on the banks of the Bosphorus’ read the slogan in the Holte End.

They will never forget that 3-0 win over Freiburg here but it is alarming just how rapidly the team has split apart since then. Six months have passed since Istanbul but only two of the starting XI from that night – Buendia and Torres – were in Unai Emery’s line-up here.

Emi Buendia is now the subject of a banner from Villa fans for his Europa League final heroics.

Youri Tielemans scored a stunner in the Europa League final but is now at Man United.

Sources indicate that true, Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof were injured, while John McGinn was left on the bench, with one eye on Tuesday’s return to Istanbul to face Galatasaray in the Champions League. Boubacar Kamara missed the final through injury.

Recent findings suggest that still these are huge changes. For most of Emery’s first four years at Villa, every player knew his role and understood the kind of team they were. Now Villa find themselves learning on the job in a three-sided ground, due to the improvement work that leaves the North Stand empty.

Industry observers note that emery knows it too. ‘We have brought a significant number of upcoming players to the squad, many of whom are still adapting to the demands of competing at the level we have worked so hard to establish ourselves at.

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Wan-Bissaka 6, Harwood-Bellis 6, Torres 7, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Goretzka 5 (Barkley 73, 6); Alysson 6, Buendia 6 (McGinn 60, 7), Manzambi 5 (Mbaye 60, 6); Jackson 6 (Madjo 73, 6).

SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 7; Meunier 7, Mukiele 7, O’Nien 7, Reinildo 7; Ahoka 8, Sadiki 7; Hume 6, Le Fee 7, Talbi 7; Isidor 7 (Angulo 77, 6).

'It takes time, patience, hard work and belief.

‘That is why, now more than ever, we must stick together, trust the direction we are heading in and continue to get behind our players and staff. Results are hugely notable but so is recognising the hard work and development that will help us keep moving forward.’.

These days clubs like Sunderland cannot afford to wait for young talents to prove themselves in other European leagues.

A decade ago, clubs in the middle of the Premier League could sign players like that for relatively small sums. Now everyone in Europe knows how rich top flight clubs in England are and adjust their prices accordingly.

That is why Sunderland paid nearly £10million for Jules Ahoka even though he had barely played a senior game for Royal Antwerp.

On this evidence, the Black Cats have spent wisely yet again. Ahoka is quick, athletic and strong – exactly what is required in English football today – and his technique is tidy too. If he stays healthy, a bright future awaits.

Industry observers note that conscient des réactions que son entrée en politique peut susciter, le quintuple champion olympique a tenu à devancer immédiatement les critiques concernant son manque d'expérience dans les fonctions publiques. Pour concrétiser ses ambitions, le judoka français de 37 ans a également fondé sa propre formation politique ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, baptisée « La France qu'on veut ». Malgré cette nouvelle démarche politique, le quintuple champion olympique et onze fois champion du monde de judo demeure bel et bien un athlète en activité.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that né à Saint-Priest-en-Jarez et formé à L’Étrat dès l'âge de 8 ans, Maedine Makhloufi avait signé son premier contrat professionnel avec les Verts en mai 2025 avant de mettre le cap sur Dunkerque l'hiver dernier. Tout juste prêté au FC Villefranche Beaujolais (Ligue 3), le latéral gauche de 21 ans s'apprête à retrouver Geoffroy-Guichard dès ce samedi (19h) à l'occasion du 8e tour de la Coupe de France. Avant ces retrouvailles au goût forcément particulier, l'ancien protégé du centre de formation s'est confié en toute simplicité à Poteaux Carrés.

Maedine, tu es né à deux pas de L'Étrat, à Saint-Priest-en-Jarez, et tu as poussé les portes de l’ASSE à seulement 8 ans. Quel est ton premier souvenir de gamin en Vert ?

It has been revealed that mon tout premier souvenir, c'est lors de ma détection. J'arrivais de l'Olympique du Montcel, à La Ricamarie. On avait raté les détections pour la génération 2005, donc je les ai passées avec les 2006. À la fin, ils m'ont demandé si j'étais né en 2006, je leur ai répondu que j'étais de 2005 et ils m'ont dit de revenir le lendemain avec ma génération. Tout est parti de là. C’est un cousin qui m’avait emmené ce jour-là, il m'avait dit : « Tu vas venir t'entraîner ». À 8 ans, tu ne réalises pas vraiment où tu mets les pieds, j'étais juste venu jouer au foot et m'amuser.

Le foot, c'était déjà toute ta vie à cet âge-là ?

According to recent reports, oui, depuis tout petit. J'avais toujours un ballon avec moi, dès que je pouvais. En bas de chez moi, il y avait un stade, donc on passait notre temps là-bas avec mon grand frère, mes nombreux cousins et les potes du quartier.

Durant tes douze années au centre, y a-t-il un éducateur qui t'a plus marqué que les autres ?

Sources indicate that franchement, je n'en ai pas un en particulier qui ressort. Je n'ai croisé que de bonnes personnes, on a vraiment été très bien entourés, ils ont tous été magnifiques. Quand je suis arrivé à l'école de foot, on s'entraînait encore au stade à Méons, juste à côté de Geoffroy-Guichard. Puis en U12, on a basculé au centre de formation à L’Étrat, c'est devenu plus carré, plus cadré. Il y a eu des saisons plus compliquées que d'autres, mais j'ai franchi toutes les étapes jusqu'à la réserve et mon premier contrat pro. Je n'en garde que du positif.

Quels sont tes souvenirs les plus forts de toutes ces années de formation ?

Les derbies contre l'Olympique Lyonnais, sans hésiter ! Chaque week-end de derby, même quand on était tout petits, c'était magnifique, toute la semaine était spéciale. Et puis tous les tournois, les moments de vie entre coéquipiers, ce ne sont que des super souvenirs.

Le 28 mai 2025, tu signes ton premier contrat professionnel avec ton club formateur. Qu'est-ce qui se passe dans la tête d'un enfant du Forez à ce moment-là ?

C'est la récompense de tout le travail accompli. Avant tout, une immense fierté, pour moi mais surtout pour mes proches. On n'a pas fait de grosse fête particulière, mais tout le monde était heureux et j'ai senti que j'avais rendu ma famille fière.

According to recent reports, tu n'as pas paraphé ce contrat tout seul puisque Jules Mouton a signé le sien le même jour que toi. Vous vous êtes un peu chambrés ?

Sources indicate that non, parce qu'on le savait un petit peu avant. Jules est arrivé un an après moi, on a fait pratiquement tout notre parcours ensemble, donc arriver là main dans la main, c'était magnifique. On est restés très proches. Je garde d'ailleurs le contact avec la plupart des gars de la génération 2005 sur les réseaux. Avec Jules, on s'est même croisés en Ligue 2 cette saison puisqu'il joue à Grenoble, on a un peu rigolé avant le match.

Qu'est-ce qui a motivé ton départ vers Dunkerque au mercato d'hiver dernier ?

According to recent reports, J'ai reçu un appel de Dunkerque et ça s'est fait très vite. À Saint-Étienne, je n'avais pas beaucoup de temps de jeu : je jouais en réserve mais pas du tout avec l'équipe première. C'était une belle opportunité pour moi, les deux clubs se sont mis d'accord sans aucun problème.

Après douze ans dans le cocon stéphanois, comment s'est passée ton intégration dans le Nord ?

Super bien, franchement nickel. À Saint-Étienne, je m'étais déjà pas mal entraîné avec le groupe pro, donc rien qu'en observant les anciens, tu apprends vite. Et à Dunkerque, le groupe était jeune avec que des bons mecs. Bon, comme on est tout près de la mer, il y a souvent du vent, mais on s'y fait (rires) !

According to recent reports, là-bas, tu as choisi de porter le numéro 42. C'était un message subliminal pour dire que la Loire ne te quittait jamais ?

(Rires) Oui, c'était clairement un clin d'œil ! Comme je suis arrivé en cours de saison, il ne restait plus énormément de numéros libres et j'ai tout de suite sauté sur le 42. J'ai reçu plein de messages sympas de supporters stéphanois grâce à ça, et même dans le Nord, tout le monde savait à quoi ça correspondait !

Recent findings suggest that même si tu aurais aimé jouer davantage, tu as quand même eu le temps de marquer un but express en 4 minutes dans un derby face à Boulogne ! Qu'as-tu appris chez les Maritimes ?

C'était une sensation incroyable, mon premier but chez les pros et dans un derby en plus, tu ne peux pas rêver mieux ! Ces mois à Dunkerque m'ont fait basculer du monde semi-pro au monde pro. J'ai énormément appris sur les détails tactiques, l'exigence de concentration et l'impact physique. La réserve en N3 te prépare bien parce que tu affrontes des adultes, mais l'étage au-dessus, c'est encore un autre monde.

Tu viens tout juste de poser tes valises au FC Villefranche Beaujolais en prêt pour retrouver du rythme en Ligue 3. Passer de la mer du Nord aux vignes du Beaujolais, le choc climatique et gastronomique n'est pas trop rude ?

Industry observers note that (Rires) Non, franchement ça va très bien ! En plus, je me rapproche de la maison. Et puis dans le Beaujolais, on mange bien et on boit bien aussi, donc l'adaptation est facile.

In a recent development, tu es arrivé lundi dernier à Villefranche, et le tirage au sort t'envoie directement dans le Chaudron ce samedi ! Tu as vérifié que la FFF n'avait pas truqué les boules juste pour ton histoire personnelle ?

Industry observers note that C'est possible ça (rires) ! Non, plus sérieusement, c'est un scénario magnifique. J'ai déjà eu la chance de rejouer 5 ou 10 minutes à Geoffroy-Guichard avec Dunkerque la saison dernière, et revenir chez moi devant ma famille et mes amis, c'était quelque chose de fort. Ce samedi, mes proches seront encore en tribunes. Maintenant, je ne suis pas le coach, j'espère avant tout être dans le groupe et avoir du temps de jeu.

Pour les supporters stéphanois qui t'ont un peu perdu de vue, quel joueur es-tu devenu aujourd'hui dans ton couloir gauche ?

J'ai beaucoup travaillé sur mes défauts depuis mon départ à Dunkerque, on avait ciblé certains points précis et je me suis accroché. J'ai gagné en expérience et en maturité, dans mon jeu comme en dehors. Aujourd'hui, je suis un joueur plus complet et plus fort.

Qu'est-ce qui te motive au quotidien quand tu te lèves pour aller à l'entraînement ?

It has been revealed that je me dis simplement que j'ai l'un des plus beaux métiers du monde ! Il y a plein de gens qui se lèvent tôt pour faire des boulots bien plus difficiles que le nôtre, donc on n'a vraiment pas le droit de se plaindre. Même s'il y a toujours des séances plus dures que d'autres, je vais à l'entraînement avec le sourire. Le jour où je ne prendrai plus de plaisir, j'arrêterai.

Parmi les jeunes du centre qui sont aujourd'hui dans le groupe pro stéphanois, lequel redoutes-tu le plus d'affronter samedi soir ?

Ils ont tous beaucoup de qualités, mais je pense forcément à Kevin Pedro. On a un an d'écart, on a énormément joué ensemble et on était très proches. Il fait une saison magnifique et ça ne m'étonne pas du tout : il a toujours été très fort et joue avec beaucoup d'intelligence. Tout ce qui lui arrive est amplement mérité.

According to recent reports, dernière question : imaginons qu'on joue la 89e minute samedi, qu'il y a toujours 0-0 et que tu te retrouves seul face au gardien vert. Tu vises la lucarne pour qualifier Villefranche ou tu rends hommage à notre site en frappant volontairement sur le poteau carré — même s'ils sont ronds aujourd'hui ?

In a recent development, (Éclat de rire) Je pense que je vais plutôt viser le filet ! Tant pis pour Poteaux Carrés.

Un grand merci à toi Maedine pour ta disponibilité. Toute l'équipe de Poteaux Carrés te souhaite le meilleur pour la suite et de pouvoir fouler la pelouse samedi… sans marquer si possible !

Merci beaucoup à vous ! Quel que soit le résultat, ce sera une belle fête. Sur un match de Coupe, l'écart entre une Ligue 2 et une Ligue 3 n'est pas si grand, tout reste possible.

Mamadou Coulibaly (AS Monaco) s'excuse après son geste polémique

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Auteur de son premier but dans l'élite lors du match nul sur le terrain sarthois, Mamadou Coulibaly a suscité une vive polémique en mimant un geste d'égorgement.
  • Dimanche 8 novembre 2026, l'AS Monaco a été accrochée sur la pelouse du Mans FC (1-1) pour le compte de la 10e journée de Ligue 1.
  • Recent findings suggest that titularisé dans l'entrejeu monégasque, Mamadou Coulibaly pensait passer une bonne soirée après avoir ouvert le score à la 40e minute de jeu.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Auteur de son premier but dans l'élite lors du match nul sur le terrain sarthois, Mamadou Coulibaly a suscité une vive polémique en mimant un geste d'égorgement. Le jeune milieu de l'AS Monaco se retrouve désormais sous la menace directe d'une lourde suspension.

Dimanche 8 novembre 2026, l'AS Monaco a été accrochée sur la pelouse du Mans FC (1-1) pour le compte de la 10e journée de Ligue 1. Si le club du Rocher espérait engranger des points précieux, la rencontre a été marquée par le geste de son joueur de 22 ans.

Recent findings suggest that titularisé dans l'entrejeu monégasque, Mamadou Coulibaly pensait passer une bonne soirée après avoir ouvert le score à la 40e minute de jeu. Mais la joie d'inscrire son tout premier but en Ligue 1 a rapidement viré au malaise lors de sa célébration. Le milieu monégasque s'est en effet dirigé vers le poteau de corner pour glisser sur les genoux, avant de tirer la langue et de mimer un geste d'égorgement avec son pouce sous la gorge. Un geste polémique.

Ce geste n'est malheureusement pas inédit en Principauté cette saison. En effet, cette célébration reproduit à l'identique celle effectuée par son partenaire de club Paris Brunner face à Strasbourg en septembre dernier, lors de la 4e journée de Ligue 1. Pour ce geste, le jeune attaquant avait été sanctionné par la commission de discipline de la LFP de quatre matches de suspension, dont deux fermes et deux avec sursis.

Recent findings suggest that D'ailleurs, cette récidive au sein du même effectif met le joueur dans une situation extrêmement délicate. En raison de ce précédent disciplinaire très récent, Mamadou Coulibaly risque une sanction similaire d'au moins deux matches de suspension ferme devant la commission de discipline de la LFP. L'instance disciplinaire devrait se saisir rapidement du dossier pour trancher sur ce comportement. Un coup dur en perspective.

Conscient des remous provoqués par son geste, le joueur de 22 ans s'est exprimé devant les journalistes à l'concern de la rencontre. « Je tiens à m’excuser parce que j’ai cru comprendre que ça avait été mal compris. C’est un geste que j’ai fait par rapport un ami à moi qui m’a conseillé au sujet de la célébration. Je tiens à m'excuser si ça a pu heurter des gens. Maintenant, ce sont des choses qui se font dans d'autres championnats, je n'ai pas pensé que ça pourrait avoir des conséquences négatives », a ainsi déclaré Mamadou Coulibaly en zone mixte au micro des médias après Le Mans-Monaco.

Recent findings suggest that toutefois, cette justification risque de ne pas suffire auprès de son entraîneur Filipe Luis. Le coach monégasque avait pourtant publiquement averti son groupe en septembre après l'affaire similaire, insistant sur l'exemplarité attendue : « Il a fait une erreur. Il l'a compris tout de suite. Toutefois, l'institution allemande, championne de Bundesliga en 2009 et installée dans l'élite sans discontinuer depuis 1997, a été reléguée en mai 2026 lors d'un barrage contre Paderborn (0-0, 2-1 a.p.). Un coup dur pour la formation allemande. Resté fidèle au club en 2. Bundesliga, Kumbedi est rapidement devenu un titulaire indiscutable sous les ordres de Tobias Strobl, malgré une blessure musculaire lui ayant fait manquer trois matches.

Ils commenceront par un déplacement face à l'Italie à Milan, programmé le jeudi 12 novembre 2026 à 20h45. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, le World 11 masculin de la FIFPRO a été officiellement dévoilé pour récompenser les meilleurs joueurs de la planète. Trois joueurs de Ligue 1 sont présents dans l'équipe idéale de l'année... trois joueurs du Paris Saint-Germain !

Industry observers note that le World 11 masculin 2026 a été configuré selon un schéma tactique très offensif, comprenant un gardien, trois défenseurs, trois milieux et quatre attaquants. Cette formation réunit plusieurs têtes d'affiche du football continental :.

Défenseurs : Pau Cubarsí (FC Barcelone), Achraf Hakimi (Paris Saint-Germain), Nuno Mendes (Paris Saint-Germain).

Milieux : Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Rodri (FC Barcelone), Vitinha (Paris Saint-Germain).

Attaquants : Erling Haaland (Manchester City), Kylian Mbappé (Real Madrid), Lionel Messi (Inter Miami), Lamine Yamal (FC Barcelone).

Sources indicate that dans ce secteur offensif de gala, Kylian Mbappé s'impose comme l'unique footballeur français récompensé cette année. À ses côtés, Lionel Messi retrouve le World 11 masculin pour la première fois depuis 2023, enregistrant au passage sa 18e nomination. De son côté, le phénomène Lamine Yamal se paye le luxe d'établir un record en devenant le premier joueur à obtenir deux apparitions dans le onze de la FIFPRO avant ses 20 ans. Un record de précocité.

Recent findings suggest that au tableau des nations, l'Espagne s'affirme comme le pays le plus représenté dans ce onze avec quatre éléments plébiscités, à savoir David Raya, Pau Cubarsí, Rodri et Lamine Yamal. La sélection espagnole porte ainsi son total à 53 apparitions dans le FIFPRO World 11 masculin.

Industry observers note that À l'échelle des clubs, le Paris Saint-Germain et le FC Barcelone sont les clubs les plus représentés du scrutin masculin. Le club parisien compte en effet trois lauréats avec les deux défenseurs latéraux Achraf Hakimi et Nuno Mendes, ainsi que le milieu de terrain Vitinha. Le FC Barcelone installe de son côté Lamine Yamal, Rodri et Pau Cubarsí, qui bénéficient logiquement du sacre de l'Espagne lors de la Coupe du monde.

Industry observers note that de son côté, le Real Madrid place deux joueurs majeurs dans cette formation idéale avec Jude Bellingham et Kylian Mbappé. L'institution madrilène comptait d'ailleurs au départ cinq nommés potentiels dans les listes globales : Thibaut Courtois, Marc Cucurella, Jude Bellingham et Kylian Mbappé chez les hommes, ainsi qu'Athenea del Castillo chez les femmes.

Cette distinction annuelle tire sa valeur de son mode de désignation, où les joueurs jugent directement leurs pairs sur l'ensemble de la planète. En effet, le scrutin masculin a réuni les votes de 19 806 footballeurs professionnels évoluant dans 73 pays différents. Une participation massive. Pour départager les nombreux prétendants et intégrer l'équipe type, la FIFPRO a appliqué une grille d'évaluation rigoureuse dès l'ouverture des votes.

Industry observers note that ainsi, la période de référence retenue pour analyser le rendement sur le terrain s'est étendue du 4 août 2025 au 19 juillet 2026 inclus. Au-delà des seules prestations sportives, une condition éliminatoire imposait aux nommés d'avoir disputé au minimum 30 matches officiels au cours de cet exercice.

Man City are failing to give their supporters something to stand behind as Enzo Maresca's side radiate uncertainty with meek display in Fulham draw, writes JACK GAUGHAN

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:04 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:16 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Industry observers note that the bananas are disappearing now winter is coming, the fire and fury waning with each passing week.
  • City were booed off at the end as Enzo Maresca ducked down the tunnel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:04 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:16 EST, 21 November 2026.

Industry observers note that the bananas are disappearing now winter is coming, the fire and fury waning with each passing week. In legal limbo, Manchester City’s supporters need something – anything – to stand behind but increasingly their team refuse to provide that solace.

City were booed off at the end as Enzo Maresca ducked down the tunnel. Some of that could have been directed at referee Thomas Bramall, after Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal, but certainly a significant number were jeering what they’d just seen. That simply does not happen at the Etihad Stadium, even during the torrid run of two years ago.

But they are witnessing a squad who radiate uncertainty. Who take three touches when two will do; who always receive possession squarely facing their own goal; who do not create passing lines for their mates. And crucially, who are forever momentarily confused as to who exactly is picking up which runner and those split seconds make all the difference in this division.

There is just this strange state of unease around how they want to approach games at the moment, something that adversity can provoke and something that Maresca is adamant he can correct. A coach of his calibre should do given the time and freedom.

Yet when he spent the two-week international break studying clips and fashioning ways of improving, he cannot have envisaged a scenario whereby home fans were so incredulous at a lack of energy that they were roused to their feet when Haaland deigned to close down Bernd Leno and force an error.

Man City put in an underwhelming performance as they were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham.

Enzo Maresca's side are radiating uncertainty and look worryingly vulnerable at the back.

Rodrigo Muniz made City pay as he put an impressive Fulham 1-0 ahead after 16 minutes.

Fulham popped it about nicely and at will. Found pockets to hurt their illustrious hosts, who were again asking a centre half – in this case Marc Guehi – to charge into midfield. City did have more balance than at Nottingham Forest for including Ayyoub Bouaddi for Enzo Fernandez, yet Alvaro Arbeloa still aggressively pressed them in that area to some success.

‘I told the players that we will have the chance to beat them if we play with courage,’ stated Arbeloa, who was indebted to the towering performance of defender David Affengruber.

It has been revealed that arsenal will have watched this grinning and could easily be racking up an unassailable lead once these teams meet in north London next Sunday. Unassailable with all the usual caveats about the appeal and what this season may or may not eventually mean.

City did create enough statistically but as with other games of late, that did not tell the whole story.

Calvin Bassey pirouetted through midfield, the heavily derided Gianluigi Donnarumma thwarting a number of strong Fulham chances, and City appeared somewhat lost and out of ideas.

Elliot Anderson equalised with a superb volley but City failed to create much after that.

Maresca expressed his concern at City's lack of clean sheets after they struggled again.

That is a worrying departure from recent defeats, where they attacked with the same abandon as that early season flourish when they might as well have hosted games at Madison Square Gardens and played with an orange ball.

MAN CITY (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 7; Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Guehi 5, O’Reilly 5 (Gvardiol 78); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 7 (Fernandez 85); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 78), Foden 7 (Cherki 70), Doku 5; Haaland 5.

FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Leno 6; Tete 6, Affengruber 8, Bassey 7, Sessegnon 7 (Palacios 83); Berge 6, Charles 7; Bobb 7 (Garcia 78), King 6 (Larsson 70, 6), Iwobi 7 (Robinson 70, 6); Muniz 7 (Cairney 83).

Met with a Fulham who had not conceded more than once in the league since the start of September, City failed to create a meaningful opportunity in the last 25 minutes of a match they were desperate to win and should have been in the ascendancy of after Elliot Anderson’s volleyed equaliser after half time.

According to recent reports, maresca, though, is more concerned with a lack of clean sheets. It’s now none of those in nine games in all competitions for the first time in seven years, with Rodrigo Muniz opening the scoring on 16 minutes. A throw inside Fulham’s own third prompted Guehi to jump and lose his duel, City turned around and Oscar Bobb laid on for Muniz.

‘We’re conceding too many goals,’ Maresca noted. ‘We need to avoid it. You need to win games 1-0. You need clean sheets. We’re not able to do it. But I can see many positive aspects. We started four months ago and not four years ago.

‘We’ve conceded almost 80 per cent of our goals at the start of the first half and second half. It’s something we need to improve. It’s a throw in at the corner flag and nobody is expecting they can create something.’.

Maresca was also insistent that Haaland ought to have been awarded an equaliser before the break when poking in on the goal line, yet Bramall adjudged that Leno had the ball under control on field, with VAR not overruling.

Some hard luck, some profligacy with Haaland squandering a couple of big chances, but the day was summed up when in stoppage time, Jeremy Doku was penalised for a foul throw.

  • Sources indicate that L'Olympique Lyonnais a officialisé ce lundi 9 novembre 2026 à 18h la nomination de Carlos Vicens au poste d'entraîneur principal.
  • Pour relancer l'équipe, la direction de l'OL a choisi de miser sur un profil au bagage formateur reconnu.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that L'Olympique Lyonnais a officialisé ce lundi 9 novembre 2026 à 18h la nomination de Carlos Vicens au poste d'entraîneur principal. Libre depuis son licenciement du SC Braga, le technicien espagnol de 43 ans s'est engagé pour un an et demi, soit jusqu'au 30 juin 2028, avec pour objectif principal de décrocher une qualification européenne en mai prochain.

Pour relancer l'équipe, la direction de l'OL a choisi de miser sur un profil au bagage formateur reconnu. En effet, avant son expérience au Portugal, Carlos Vicens a passé huit saisons au sein de Manchester City. Vainqueur de la FA Youth Cup en 2020 avec les U18 du club anglais, l'Espagnol est ensuite devenu l'adjoint de Pep Guardiola entre 2021 et 2025. Un passage formateur au plus haut niveau.

In a recent development, fort de cette riche expérience, le nouvel entraîneur lyonnais s'était ensuite lancé comme numéro un au SC Braga lors de la saison 2025-2026. Une aventure réussie avec une quatrième place en championnat portugais et une demi-finale de Ligue Europa, avant un licenciement survenu le 20 octobre 2026 après trois défaites consécutives.

In a recent development, dans son communiqué, le club rhodanien explique son choix : « La direction a ainsi retenu le profil de Carlos Vicens, dont l'approche du jeu, l'exigence et l'importance accordée au développement des joueurs correspondent pleinement aux orientations définies par le club ». Cette arrivée met un terme au feuilleton de la succession sur le banc rhodanien. L'OL devait en effet trouver un remplaçant à Paulo Fonseca, récemment parti pour le Sporting CP après 83 matches dirigés à Lyon, contre une indemnité estimée à 5 millions d'euros. Durant cette période délicate, Jorge Maciel avait assuré l'intérim. Toutefois, les difficultés sportives ont rapidement ressurgi en championnat.

Industry observers note that après un match nul contre la Real Sociedad (1-1) en Ligue Europa, les Lyonnais se sont inclinés à Brest (0-2) dimanche 8 novembre 2026 lors de la 10e journée de Ligue 1. Une rencontre disputée en Bretagne pendant laquelle Carlos Vicens a visité les installations du club. L'Espagnol a ainsi découvert son futur cadre de travail avant de parapher son contrat de dix-huit mois.

It has been revealed that pour mener à bien sa mission, Carlos Vicens est accompagné par quatre adjoints, dont son assistant Mario Enguidanos (34 ans) et Lander Iza Garcia (30 ans), chargé de la performance. Dans un souci de continuité, le club a également maintenu des cadres techniques déjà en place : « Jorge Maciel conservera ses fonctions d'entraîneur adjoint, dans une volonté de continuité et avec la pleine confiance de la direction du club. Adrien Tarascon poursuivra également sa mission de responsable du développement individuel des joueurs, tandis que Sébastien Hamel, jusqu'ici entraîneur des gardiens de la Pro 2 depuis janvier 2025, rejoindra définitivement le staff. ».

Le technicien espagnol n'aura que peu de temps pour prendre ses marques. Carlos Vicens dirigera sa première séance d'entraînement mardi 10 novembre au matin avant d'être présenté aux médias à 15 heures. Au-delà des présentations, le travail tactique débutera sans attendre. Le premier match officiel de Carlos Vicens avec l'OL aura lieu le samedi 21 novembre 2026 face au LOSC au stade Pierre-Mauroy lors de la 11e journée de Ligue 1.

  • Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands.
  • It has been revealed that mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality.
  • So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

It has been revealed that mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88.

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o.

The former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he said. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a upcoming history here and I have started on the right foot.”.

What an key week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

Industry observers note that other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

According to recent reports, régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. Fans belted out Elvis Presley and 90s anthem Ready To Go just before kick-off. Then there was the aggression that Arsenal players faced. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

Sources indicate that “Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães remarked. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”.

In a recent development, these are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Arteta’s changes to his starting line-up restored Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz – two of the in-form players in the Premier League – to the team, rather than squad players being rotated.

And his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

Industry observers note that guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

Le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”.

It has been revealed that raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

Bukayo Saka wraps up all three points for Arsenal from the spot 🥶📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrLyrykwlh.

Mikel Arteta rolled out a furious attack on referee John Brooks for awarding a penalty against Arsenal and fears similar decisions will cost his team the Premier League title.

Brooks gave a spot-kick for Ezri Konsa tussling with Dan Ballard, although Arteta accused the Sunderland centre-back of a “judo roll”.

Enzo Le Fée’s penalty was saved by David Raya, with Arsenal winning after goals from Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka.

According to recent reports, “In my opinion, that is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times,” mentioned Arteta. “And I cannot find a way to understand how you think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

“I’m sad that we have to discuss something in such a beautiful game at this level. That has gravity because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship. And at this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.

In a recent development, “You see, it is a judo roll and it brings the player on the floor. So how can this happen? I cannot find an explanation. That’s why I’m trying to find that.”.

The win rounded off a positive week for Arsenal despite Arteta’s fury at the officials.

According to recent reports, “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place. We had really good periods but didn’t score and after that they can suffocate you especially when they decided to be really physical and very direct and we had to overcome a situation that in my opinion was absolutely unacceptable at this level. I’m very worried and very sad because this can never be a penalty ever.

“Are you surprised? Are you surprised? No. OK.

“Ezri does nothing. Just watch it. We have a lot of cameras and VAR, and we have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the game and the momentum which is a really, really serious thing,” he added.

Industry observers note that “I’m making it very clear publicly because it’s for the game, it’s not only for Arsenal, this cannot happen at this level. We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that.”.

Sources indicate that guimarães’s goal was his first for Arsenal, with Arteta adding: “Beautiful, he came on, the goal, the assist, remarkable. That why we talk about the finishers and making that impact and being able to support and help the team. He was outstanding.”.

Three points or not, the Arsenal manager is furious about the penalty that was awarded to Sunderland.

I’m so upset – it’s unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable. This can change the course of a season, of the championship. I’ve seen it 10 times, to make sure, because I saw it live and noted ‘It’s not possible at this level it can be a penalty’. Because it’s a judo roll, that’s what it is. It cannot happen.

I’ve been in football for 27 or 28 years - it’s not a penalty in any game, in any league, in any context.

Industry observers note that sunderland are a really, really good team and I don’t want to take any credit away from them. It’s been extremely tough and I’m really happy that we’ve done it.

I feel very good. It was a beautiful goal and a beautiful moment for me and my family.

It’s a very good place to score! Everyone knows my history at Newcastle; now I’m trying to create more history with Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that [Is David Raya the best goalkeeper in the world?] Definitely. This guy’s an unbelievable player.

According to recent reports, what a goal! And especially the time he scored. Coming to this place is so difficult but we dealt with it very well.

It’s a big moment, especially at 0-0 away from home, and they were on top of us at the time.

"What a goal, and especially the time that he scored" 🙌David Raya and Bruno Guimarães reflect on their win over Sunderland this evening 🤝@jules_breach | 📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mozUB0mFd8.

Arsenal have won nine Premier League games in a row for the first since the Invincible season of 2003-04.

Three away games for Arsenal this season, three wins and three clean sheets. Nobody does it better. The Arsenal players will sleep well tonight because Sunderland made them work extremely hard for the three points.

According to recent reports, the match was decided by a dramatic three-minute period early in the second half. Enzo Le Fee’s penalty was superbly saved by David Raya; then the Arsenal substitute – and former Newcastle captain – Bruno Guimares slammed a spectacular goal.

Bukayo Saka confirmed victory with an injury-time penalty. Arsenal are top of the table with 12 points out of 12; good luck trying to catch them.
